newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC raises sales outlook due to Internet, intranet.
newsitem.headline: NEC raises sales outlook due to Internet, intranet.

text.p: Japanese electronics giant NEC Corp said on Thursday its sales in the current business year would be larger than previously estimated, boosted by increasing use of the Internet and intranet systems.
NEC also said it would finish restructuring its loss-making home electronics unit this business year, ending next March.

"Our parent sales will be 50 billion yen ($438 million) larger than our previous forecast as sales of telecoms equipment and computers rose due to increasing demand for Internet and intranet," NEC said in a statement.
The Internet is a vast computer interchange available to anyone with a computer and a modem, while intranets are private corporate computer networks that function much like it.

NEC now expects parent sales of 3.95 trillion yen ($34.6 billion) in the current business year, up from its previous forecast of 3.9 trillion yen ($34.2 billion). Its actual parent sales in 1995/96 were 3.45 trillion yen ($30.2 billion).

But despite the upward revision in sales, it maintained a parent current profit forecast of 105 billion yen ($921 million) as an unexpectedly large fall in semiconductor prices is likely to cap any increase. It posted parent current profit of 100.62 billion yen ($882 million) in 1995/96.
Current profit is pre-tax but includes gains and losses made on securities investments.

The expected sales rise is also seen pushing up NEC's group sales this year to 4.79 trillion yen ($42.0 billion). NEC previously said group sales in 1996/97 would be 4.75 trillion yen ($41.6 billion) against actual group sales of 4.40 trillion yen ($38.5 billion) the year before.

Group profit is combined profits at a company and its units. NEC also said an accumulated losses at NEC Home Electronics would be wiped out by the end of next March and that it would drastically reduce the unit's business.
NEC had expected its unit's accumulated deficit to have reached 130 billion yen by the end of March if restructuring measures had not been implemented.
Due to the restructuring, it will have to include an extraordinary loss of 98 billion yen ($859 million) in its 1996/97 earnings.
"We are still facing an uphill battle but we think we have just passed an important hurdle," senior vice president Shigeo Matsumoto told a news conference.
NEC also expects a special loss from its North American unit NEC Technologies, partly due to disposal of unnecessary assets following consolidation of its PC business with Packard Bell in July.
The special losses will adversely affect NEC's net profit, which would otherwise have grown, its said.

After asset sales and tax payments, NEC sees parent net profit in 1996/97 at 60 billion yen ($526 million), unchanged from its previous forecast. Its actual parent net profit in 1995/96 was 55.62 billion yen ($487 million).

NEC said raised its group net profit forecast for 1996/97 to 90 billion yen ($789 million) from its previous forecast of 60 billion yen ($526 million), up from its actual group net profit of 77.17 billion yen ($676 million). ($1=114 yen)
